title: Subscribe and manage pages, projected on the site
description:
**Milestone:** M3, public email and new stories

**Goal.** As a reader, I subscribe and manage notifications on real pages of the site, in its theme, light and dark, never on an /api URL.

**Build.**
- `src/papyrus_content/projection/standard/notifications_pages.py`, modelled on `newsletter_pages.py`: `/notifications/`, `confirm`, `confirmed`, `preferences`, `unsubscribed`, `expired`; `noindex`, no Markdown twin or sitemap entry, `<meta name="referrer" content="same-origin">`.
- External script and a web component named like the newsletter's versioned one under `/_plugins/`, no inline script, working under the strict CSP.
- Buttons, no dropdowns. Lucide icons, flat fills, no borders. State in words and marks. Sign-in option for Slack and Discord only when those channels are live and the site is a public-reader site.
- Screenshot review with Ryan before prod. Machines on Machines first.

**Acceptance.**
Ryan's screenshot approval recorded; light, dark and phone checked.

**Depends on:** PPY-44721a
**Related:** kanbus-eedbbd, kanbus-1c3618

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Reader pages
  Scenario: Subscribing on the site
    Given a site with notifications on
    When a reader opens its notifications page and enters an address
    Then the page says to check their email, in the site's own design

  Scenario: Managing
    Given a confirmed subscriber follows the manage link
    When they turn new-story email off
    Then the page confirms it in words

  Scenario: A bad link
    When someone opens a manage link that is no good
    Then they land on the site's expired page, not an /api address
```

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decisions (PR 1430): (1) Seven pages: /notifications/ (subscribe) plus confirm, confirmed, preferences, unsubscribe, unsubscribed, expired; the machine routes already redirect to these. (2) Two versioned plugin scripts: the <papyrus-notifications> web component (subscribe page only) and the pages script (all pages). (3) New read-only state kind=offered returns the site's public list settings so the component needs no inline config. (4) Lists are toggle buttons that say On/Off with bell/bell-off; no dropdowns, no borders. (5) Service 502/503 is said in words, not routed to expired (the function answers 503 until Caducus supports public audiences). (6) Slack/Discord sign-in option NOT built: those channels are not live. (7) Not deployed or released; screenshot review with Ryan (Machines on Machines first) still due before any rollout.
